questions.q:
If $\lim _{x \rightarrow} x \sin \left(\frac{1}{x}\right)=A$ and $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} x \sin \left(\frac{1}{x}\right)=B$,
then which one of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
As given,
$\mathrm{A}=\lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \infty} \mathrm{x} \sin \left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)=\lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\sin \left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)}{\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)}$
Let $\mathrm{t}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}$ when $\mathrm{x} \rightarrow \alpha, \mathrm{t} \rightarrow 0$
$\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \mathrm{A} &=\lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\sin \mathrm{t}}{\mathrm{t}}=1 \\
&\left[\because \lim _{\mathrm{t} \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin \mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{x}}=1\right]
\end{aligned}$
and $\mathrm{B}=\lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow 0} \mathrm{x} \sin $\$left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)
$\Rightarrow \$mathrm{B}=\lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow 0} \mathrm{x} \cdot \lim _{\mathrm{x} \rightarrow 0} \sin \left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{x}}\right)$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{B}=0$
$\therefore \quad A=1$ and $B=0 is correct$

questions.q: The value of $\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{x^{2}-2 x+1}{x^{2}-4 x+2}\right)^{x}$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{x^{2}-2 x+1}{x^{2}-4 x+2}\right)^{x} \\ &=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(1+\frac{2 x-1}{x^{2}-4 x+2}\right)^{x} \\ &=e^{\lim _{x \rightarrow-\infty}\left(\frac{x(2 x-1)}{x^{2}-4 x+2}\right)}=e^{2} \end{aligned}$

Hence, option (c) is correct.$

questions.solution: \$(\lim _{x \rightarrow \pi} \frac{1-\sin \frac{x}{2}}{\left(\cos \frac{x}{2}\right)\left(\cos \frac{x}{4}-\sin \frac{x}{4}\right)}$\) Let \(\quad x=\pi+h, x \rightarrow \pi, h \rightarrow 0\) \(\begin{gathered} $=\lim _{\substack{x \rightarrow \pi \\ h \rightarrow 0}} \frac{1-\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}+\frac{h}{2}\right)}{\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}+\frac{h}{2}\right)\left(\cos \left(\frac{\pi+h}{4}\right)-\sin \left(\frac{\pi+h}{4}\right)\right)}$\\ $=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{1-\cos \frac{h}{2}}{-\sin \frac{h}{2} \cdot\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{4} \cos \frac{h}{4}-\sin \frac{\pi}{4} \sin \frac{h}{4}-\sin \frac{\pi}{4} \cdot \cos \frac{h}{4}-\cos \frac{\pi}{4} \cdot \sin \frac{h}{4}\right)} \end{gathered}$\) \(\begin{aligned} & $=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sqrt{2}\left(1-\cos \frac{h}{2}\right)}{-\sin \frac{h}{2}\left\{\cos \frac{h}{4}-\sin \frac{h}{4}-\cos \frac{h}{4}-\sin \frac{h}{4}\right\}}$\\ & $=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sqrt{2}\left(1-\cos \frac{h}{2}\right)}{\sin \frac{h}{2} \cdot\left(-2 \sin \frac{h}{4}\right)}$\\ & $=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sqrt{2} \cdot 2 \sin ^2 \frac{h}{4}}{2 \cdot \sin \frac{h}{2} \times \sin \frac{h}{4}}$\\ & $=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \sqrt{2} \frac{\sin \frac{h}{4}}{\sin \frac{h}{2}}=\sqrt{2} \lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{\sin \frac{h}{4}}{4\left(\frac{h}{4}\right)} \cdot \frac{2(h / 2)}{\sin \frac{h}{2}}$\\ & $=\sqrt{2} \times \frac{2}{4} \cdot \lim _{h \rightarrow 0}  \left(\frac{\sin \frac{h}{4}}{\frac{h}{4}}\right)\left(\frac{\frac{h}{2}}{\sin \frac{h}{2}}\right)$\\ \text{ and } $=\sqrt{2} \times \frac{2}{4} \times$1 \times $1=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}$\)$

questions.q: If $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2}{x - 3}, g\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x - 3}{x + 4}$ and $h\left(x\right) = - \dfrac{2\left(2x + 1\right)}{x^{2} + x - 12}$,~then $\lim_{x \to 3} \left[f  \left($x\right) + g \left(x\right) + h\left(x\right)\right]$ is$
questions.solution:
Given:& $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2}{x - 3}, g\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x - 3}{x + 4}$ and $h\left(x\right) = - \dfrac{2\left(2x + 1\right)}{x^{2} + x - 12} = - \dfrac{2\left(2x + 1\right)}{\left(x - 3\right)\left(x + 4\right)}$.

We have $f\left(x\right) + g\left(x\right) + h\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x^{2} - 4x + 17 - 4x - 2}{x^{2} + x - 12}$

$= \dfrac{x^{2} - 8x + 15}{x^{2} + x - 12} = \dfrac{ \left(x - 3\$right)\left(x - 5\right)}{ \left(x - 3\right)\left($x + 4\right)} = \left($x - 5\right)\left(x + 4\right)$

Now~$\lim_{x \to 3} \left[f \left($x\right) + g \left(x\right) + h\left(x\right)\right]$

$= \lim_{x \to 3}\left(x - 5\$right)\left($x + 4\right) = - \dfrac{2}{7}$

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{cos x + sin x - \dfrac{1}{1 - x}}{3x^{2}} \left(\dfrac{0}{0}\right) [using L'hospital rule]

Let $a>0$ be a real number. Then the limit $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2} \frac{a^{x}+a^{3-x}-\left(a^{2}+a\right)}{a^{3-x}-a^{x / 2}}$
is
questions.solution: $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2} \frac{a^{x}+a^{3-x}-\left(a^{2}+a\right)}{a^{3-x}-a^{x / 2}}\lim _{x \rightarrow 2} \frac{\left(a^{x}-a\right)\left(a^{x / 2}-a\right)\left(a^{x / 2}+a\right)}{\left(a-a^{x / 2}\right)\left(a^{2}+a^{x}+a^{x / 2} \cdot a\right)}\lim _{x \rightarrow 2}-\frac{\left(a^{x}-a\right)\left(a^{x / 2}+a\right)}{a^{2}+a^{x}+a^{x / 2} \cdot a}=\frac{2}{3}(1-a)$

questions.q: The value of $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{cos\left(tan ⁡ x\right) - cos ⁡ x}{4x^{4}}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$cos \left($tan ⁡ x\right) - cos ⁡ x = 2sin \left(\dfrac{x + tan ⁡ x}{2}\right)sin \left(\dfrac{x - tan ⁡ x}{2}\right)
$⇒ \lim_{x \to $0}\dfrac{cos\left(tan ⁡ x\right) - cos ⁡ x}{4x^{4}} = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{2sin\left(\dfrac{x + tan ⁡ x}{2}\right)sin\left(\dfrac{x - tan ⁡ tan ⁡ x}{2}\right)}{4x^{4}}
$= \lim_{x \to $0}\dfrac{2sin \left(\dfrac{x + tan ⁡ x}{2}\right)sin \left(\dfrac{x - tan ⁡ x}{2}\right)}{4x^{4} \left(\dfrac{x + tan ⁡ x}{2}\right) \left(\dfrac{x - tan ⁡ x}{2}\right)} $\$left(\dfrac{x^{2} - tan^{2}x}{4}\right)
$= $\dfrac{1}{8}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{x^{2} - tan^{2}x}{x4}
$= $\dfrac{1}{8}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{x^{2} - \left(x + \dfrac{x3}{3} + \dfrac{2}{15}x^{5} + . . . .\right)2}{x4}
$= $\dfrac{1}{8}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{1}{x2}\left($1 - \left(1 + $\dfrac{x2}{3} + \dfrac{2}{15}$x^{4} + . . . .\right)2\right) = - \dfrac{1}{12}$

questions.q: The value of $\lim_{x \to {1}^{-}} ⁡ \dfrac{\sqrt{2\pi} - \sqrt{4\sin^{- 1} ⁡ x}}{\sqrt{1 - x}}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We have, $\lim_{x \to {1}^{-}} ⁡ \dfrac{\left(\sqrt{\pi} - \sqrt{2\sin^{- 1} ⁡ x}\right)}{\sqrt{1 - x}}\sqrt{2}$
$= \lim_{x \to {1}^{-}} ⁡ \dfrac{\sqrt{\pi} - \sqrt{2\sin^{- 1} ⁡ x}}{\sqrt{1 - x}} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{\pi} + \sqrt{2\sin^{- 1} ⁡ x}}{\sqrt{\pi} + \sqrt{2\sin^{- 1} ⁡ x}} \times \sqrt{2}$
$= \lim_{x \to {1}^{-}} ⁡ \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{- 1} ⁡ x\right)}{\sqrt{1 - x}\left(\sqrt{\pi} + \sqrt{2\sin^{- 1} ⁡ x}\right)}$
$= \lim_{x \to {1}^{-}} ⁡ \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}\cos^{- 1} ⁡ x}{\sqrt{1 - x}} ⋅ \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{\pi}}$
$= \lim_{\theta \to {0}^{+}} ⁡ \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}\theta}{\sqrt{2}sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)} ⋅ \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{\pi}}$ [Putting $x = cos ⁡ \theta$ ]
$= \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{2\pi}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}}$

questions.q: The value of $\lim_{x \to 1}\dfrac{xtan\left\{x\right\}}{x - 1}$ is equal to (where \left\{x\right\}$ denotes the fractional part of $x$)$
questions.solution:
$LHL = \lim_{x \to {1}^{-}}\dfrac{xtan\left\{x\right\}}{x - 1}$
Let, $x = 1 - h, asx \to {1}^{-}, h \to {0}^{+}$
$⇒ LHL = \lim_{h \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{\left(1 - h\right)tan\left\{1 - h\right\}}{- h}$
$∴ LHL = \lim_{h \to {0}^{+}}\left(1 - h\right)- htan\left(1\right) = - \infty$
Now, $RHL = \lim_{x \to {1}^{+}}\dfrac{xtan\left\{x\right\}}{x - 1}$
Let, $x = 1 + h, asx \to {1}^{+}, h \to {0}^{+}$
$⇒ RHL = \lim_{h \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{\left(1 + h\right)tan\left\{1 + h\right\}}{h}$
$⇒ RHL = \lim_{h \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{ \left(1 + h\right)tanh}{h} = \lim_{h \to {0}^{+}}\left(1 + h\right)$
$∴ RHL = \left(1 + 0\right) = 1$
Since, $LHL \ne RHL$
$∴$ the limit of the function does not exist at $x = 1$
